pairs.difference: A: ball whites stay grey-neutral, and the cast shadow on the sand turns plum, so a cool hue rests the orange. B: whites go cream and peach toward the bottom panels, and the cast shadow left of the ball is saturated orange-red, the same family as the sand.
pairs.fix: Keep the white panels clean, slightly cool white all the way down. Make the shadow on the sand a muted plum-brown, not red-orange.

pairs.difference: Both cards have loud orange wood, an orange bear, a red panel and a pure blue target against green. B's shelf underside and frame shadows run red, while A's lime wall exceeds the real background chroma slightly. These faults offset, so hue and chroma give no clear reason to choose.

A: unit body is near-neutral white with a blue side plane, on a muted sage wall, like the real computer's cool side. B: the whole body is tinted lavender and the wall flares into yellow-lime at left, so even the neutral object has a pushed hue.
pairs.fix: Paint the unit plain off-white with a soft grey-blue side. Keep the wall an even muted sage green with no yellow glow.

pairs.difference: A: sand drifts to lavender-grey, the chest's shadow side and lid interior go plum, and the lens keeps a neutral grey mass that rests the eye. B: sand, wood, coins and frame all sit in orange, with orange-red shadows on the sand and a brown-red lid interior, so the card is pulled warm.
pairs.fix: Make the sand paler and slightly grey-violet in shadow. Turn the shadow side of the chest and the lid interior a dark cool plum, not orange-brown.

pairs.difference: A: the wall is a saturated orange-red, the floor is orange, and even the shadow under the cap stays orange, so the lens has about two hue families (2.15). B: the brown wood is muted, with plum-grey floor shadows and a duller navy that give neutral rest around the white crown.
pairs.fix: Mute the wall to a dull brown wood. Make the floor shadow a soft grey-plum, and reduce the orange overall.

pairs.difference: A: the red leans crimson, with gold crowns as the one accent, a charcoal base and a green-dark cast shadow on the floor. B: the red is hotter and more orange across every face (subject chroma 0.1545, above real range), the crowns are dull, and the cast shadow nearly disappears into a glowing lime floor.
pairs.fix: Use a deeper crimson red on the booth, with bright gold crowns as the only accent. Add a dark green shadow on the floor and keep the base neutral charcoal.

pairs.difference: A: cuffs are near-black neutral, the red stays one local family and the wood is plain orange-tan. B: the gloves wash into salmon-pink with orange hot spots, the cuffs read dark red, and a saturated red rim runs along the floor shadow.
pairs.fix: Keep the gloves one rich red without pink or orange patches. Make the wrist bands plain matte black and the floor shadow a soft brown.

pairs.difference: A: yellow fins with neutral charcoal blades and greyed plum boots give a muted rest area against the violet. B: fins are pushed to orange with a hot orange rim, the blades read warm brown in the lens, and the boots use the same pure purple as the hotter magenta-violet background (0.2569).
pairs.fix: Paint the fins clean yellow with no orange edge. Make the blades neutral charcoal, the boots a dull grey-plum, and the background a calmer violet.

pairs.difference: A: posts, deck and shadows all stay orange-brown, sitting on turquoise sea and bright sand, the same mix as the generated lighthouse sea. Wood shadows never leave orange. B: underwater posts and dock shadows drop to a rich blue-charcoal, so shadow hue is related to the water.
pairs.fix: Shift the shadow under the dock and the submerged posts to dark blue-teal. Make the sea a deeper, less turquoise blue.

pairs.difference: A: hot magenta is at full push (background 0.2136, above real range), the trunk is pure orange and the palm's shadow on the sand is orange with no hue shift. B: the pink is lighter and less loud, the rocks are near-neutral, and rock shadows pick up pink from the background.
pairs.fix: Lower the magenta to a softer pink. Add pale neutral stones and tint the sand shadows slightly pink-violet instead of orange.

pairs.difference: A: lavender-grey wall and pale wood are muted so the orange locker alone is loud (background 0.1036), and the wall shadow is deep violet. B: the wall is a solid pure purple, the locker is flat pure orange, and the books are primary red, blue and green, so everything shouts at equal level.
pairs.fix: Make the wall a dusty grey-lavender. Give the locker a mellow yellow-orange and the book spines dull, mixed colors rather than pure red, blue and green.

pairs.difference: A: lime slide at 0.1759 chroma exceeds real range, with pure yellow rail and pure blue supports, four loud hues on one object. B: slide and support share one calmer green, so the hero is less loud. A's lilac tile shadows are good, which keeps this low confidence.
pairs.fix: Use a calmer mid green for the slide. Reduce the yellow to a dull straw tone and the supports to a soft blue.

pairs.difference: A: blue-violet background with a yellow body, a simple complementary pair with one mass each. B: the background pushes to hotter magenta-purple (0.2535) and the body runs to deep orange at the bottom edge, adding a warm red-orange shadow.
pairs.fix: Shift the background toward blue-violet. Keep the player body yellow with a soft golden shadow, not red-orange.

pairs.difference: A: deeper green with a darker vignette, and the envelope's shadow edge picks up pale green, so it relates to the background. B: brighter, louder green (0.2372), a warm peach-cream envelope with a warm grey-brown shadow, and a hot pink stamp.
pairs.fix: Darken the green toward the corners. Make the envelope a paler neutral cream with green-tinted shadows, and mute the stamp pink.

pairs.difference: A: melon is a crimson red and the fruit sits within the warm tone of the backdrop. B: melon and oranges are pushed to red-orange (subject 0.1696, above real range) against a duller wood (0.0937, below real range), with an olive-grey shadow mass, so the hero is much louder than the background.
pairs.fix: Paint the watermelon a deeper pink-red and calm the oranges. Keep a warm, clean, slightly brighter tabletop with brown shadows.

pairs.difference: A: cobalt door dominates, with navy shading and little warm area (warm share 0.281). B: cream wall, peach paving and an orange arch raise warm share to 0.535, the cream and peach bias seen on generated cards. Its teal leaf shadows are good, which keeps this low confidence.
pairs.fix: Make the wall a plainer, greyer off-white and the paving a neutral stone grey. Reduce the orange on the door frame to a muted brown.

pattern: Generated cards pull colors toward pure hue: whites and neutrals turn cream, peach or lavender, wood and leather go orange, backgrounds run hotter, and cast shadows stay orange-red. Real cards keep true neutrals, such as grey-white and charcoal, and let shadows shift to plum, blue or a hue related to the background, so one quiet mass rests the eye.
